name: Tempester n°75: indexed SysEx command 47 = one Sound stored into a given beat and pad of the project in RAM, answered by a status message (needs n°74)
explanation: F0 01 28 47 bb pp <152 bytes> F7, the reply of request 46 (n°74), so a Sound fetched that way goes back unchanged: the 152 bytes are the body of a 60 message. They are read, unpacked, checked against the parameter maxima (a value above its maximum becomes its default) and written to beat bb (0-15), pad pp (0-31) by the machine's own 60 receiver, given the slot instead of the selection; then the follow-up of a received 60 for that slot: Voice Assign reservations and play states of that beat, and for the beat and pad the screen shows, the beat-wide values and the LEDs. Answer F0 01 28 4F 47 00 F7; out of range: nothing written, F0 01 28 4F 47 01 F7. A shorter message never runs; bytes after the 154th are dropped. RAM only: nothing is saved to flash until the user saves the beat or project; the selection and the Revert copy are untouched. It writes its own entry, 0x47 with 154 argument bytes, in n°74's table, which n°74 leaves erased. Proof: tools/sim_indexed_sysex.py. Docs/analyses/study-indexed-sysex.md.

commands.F0 01 28 47 bb pp <152 bytes> F7: store the Sound into beat bb (0-15), pad pp (0-31); reply F0 01 28 4F 47 00 F7, or F0 01 28 4F 47 01 F7 when out of range (nothing written)

edits.why: jal [address] ; next SysEx byte: the beat
jal [address] ; next SysEx byte: the pad
jal 0x9d07c164 ; status: index out of range, nothing written
jal [address] ; the 152 bytes unpacked, checked against the parameter maxima, written to the slot (as a received 60)
jal [address] ; what follows a received 60: voices, play states, and for the shown beat and pad the cache and LEDs
.word 0x009aa300 ; command 0x47 in the indexed command table: 154 argument bytes (beat, pad, Sound), handler at the low half 0xa300
